name: Exenatide
route_note: subcutaneous injection twice daily (Byetta) or once weekly extended-release microspheres (Bydureon)

discovery.by: John Eng (Bronx Veterans Affairs Medical Center)
discovery.note: Exendin-4 was isolated from the venom (saliva) of the Gila monster, Heloderma suspectum.

tagline: The first GLP-1 drug, copied from a peptide in Gila monster venom
summary: Exenatide is a synthetic version of exendin-4, a peptide found in Gila monster venom that activates the GLP-1 receptor but resists breakdown by DPP-4. Approved in 2005 as Byetta, it was the first GLP-1 receptor agonist and opened the incretin era that led to semaglutide and tirzepatide.
mechanism: Exenatide shares about 53% sequence identity with human GLP-1 and binds the GLP-1 receptor on pancreatic beta cells, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing inappropriate glucagon release and slowing gastric emptying.

Because its N-terminal sequence is not a DPP-4 substrate, it lasts hours rather than minutes; the weekly form encapsulates it in biodegradable poly(lactide-co-glycolide) microspheres. Central effects reduce appetite and modestly lower body weight.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as adjunct to diet and exercise (adults; Bydureon BCise also in children 10 years and older)

history.title: Exendin-4 discovered
history.detail: John Eng isolates exendin-4 from Gila monster venom.

history.title: Byetta approved
history.detail: FDA approves Byetta in April 2005, the first GLP-1 receptor agonist.

history.title: Pancreatitis reports
history.detail: FDA alerts prescribers to post-marketing reports of acute pancreatitis.

history.title: Weekly Bydureon
history.detail: FDA approves once-weekly Bydureon in January 2012; Bristol-Myers Squibb acquires Amylin and AstraZeneca later takes over the franchise.

history.title: EXSCEL
history.detail: The EXSCEL trial shows once-weekly exenatide is non-inferior but not superior to placebo for cardiovascular events.

history.title: BCise autoinjector
history.detail: FDA approves the Bydureon BCise autoinjector.

pk.bioavailability: about 65–76% after SC injection (animal and human data)

safety.boxed_warning: Extended-release exenatide: risk of thyroid C-cell tumours (rodent data); contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

facts: Exenatide was developed from a peptide in the saliva of the Gila monster, a venomous lizard of the southwestern US.
Byetta (2005) was the first approved GLP-1 receptor agonist.
